texts.facts: This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 25.09.2018 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal ( 'MACT' for short), Court of Small Causes at Bengaluru, in MVC No.4580/2017. 2. This appeal is premised on the ground of inadequacy of compensation. 3. The brief facts of the case are as under: On 23.02.2017, the claimant-Smt, Saraswathi @ K. Saraswathi was traveling in APSRTC Bus bearing No.AP.04.Y.6715 on NH-42 as an inmate passenger. While the said bus was being driven at about 01.15 p.m., near Kalupalli Village, Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, the driver of the said bus drove the bus with high speed and in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety and dashed against the on-coming lorry bearing Registration No. TN.28.AR.4129, as a result of which, claimant sustained grievous injuries. Immediately thereafter, claimant was shifted to Palamner Government Hospital, where she was treated as an inpatient and thereafter she was shifted to CMC Hospital at Vellur, where she obtained treatment as an inpatient. Thereafter, she was discharged with an advise to take regular follow-up treatment. It is the case of the Smt. Saraswathi @ K. Saraswathi vs The National Insurance Company Ltd on 19 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98931947/ 2 claimant that, while being inpatient, she spent lot of money for her treatment and due to the accident, she has suffered permanent disability affecting her future earning capacity and her day-to- day functional capacity. She further states that, due to the injuries suffered in the said accident, she is unable to do her regular work, as she was able to do prior to occurrence of accident and in view of the injuries suffered by her in the accident in question, she filed a claim petition seeking compensation, against the respondents. 4. On service of notice, the respondents appeared and filed their detailed statement of objections. However, Respondent No.2 did not represent despite service of notice and was placed ex-parte. Respondent No.1 took-up a plea inter alia denying issuance of Insurance Policy and further contended that, the liability if any, would be in terms of the conditions of the policy. It was further pleaded that, the accident in question has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of APSRTC Bus and that a false case is filed against driver of the bus by colluding with the jurisdictional police. It is also pleaded that the driver of offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective Driving Licence as on the date of occurrence of accident in question and that the driver of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy. Whereas, Respondent No.3 in the statement of objections has denied occurrence of accident due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle. However, he admitted that he had hired the offending vehicle viz., the APSRTC Bus, belonging to Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the vehicle and the same was insured with the 1st respondent and the Insurance Policy was valid as on the date of occurrence of accident in question. It is further pleaded that, if at all any liability would be fastened, it has to be on Respondent No.1-Insurance Company, with which the insurance policy was in force. It is also contended by Respondent No.3 that the claim petition is liable to be dismissed for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary and proper parties. 5. On the basis of the said pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal has framed the relevant issues for consideration. 6. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Eleven documents as Exs.P1 to P10. The claimant also examined the Doctor by name Dr. Shivaprakash as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P11 to P14. 7. On the other hand, the respondent examined one M.Dasharatha as RW.1, who is the driver of APSRTC Bus. But, however he did not produce any documents on their behalf. However, in view of the Insurance Policy being in force, Respondent No.1, who is the insurer of offending vehicle, was directed to deposit the compensation amount Smt. Saraswathi @ K. texts.arguments: Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant and the learned counsel for the respondent/Insurer and the Respondent-APSRTC Corporation, the point that would arise before this Court is, - "Whether the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is meager and calling for interference by this Court,, and whether enhancement is warranted in the present facts and circumstances of this case." However, the learned counsel for the Insurer-Respondent No.1 has seriously disputed the disability to an extent of 28% opined by the Doctor, it affirms the judgment and award made by the Tribunal with regard to calculation of disability at 8%. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant has vehemently contended that the Tribunal has grossly erred in assessing meager income of Rs.8,000/- per month without appreciating the material evidence placed on record. Admittedly, in the case on hand, no material in proof of income has been placed by the claimant. In the absence of the same, the Tribunal has assessed the income to be at Rs.8,000/- per month. 13. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant that the assessment of income made by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the same calls for interference by this Court for the reason that, in the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal and this Court are left with no other alternative, but to do standard guess work.
